criteria.evidence: All four named properties hold and are enforced fail-closed by a bite-proven, CI-blocking gate. I ran both halves myself at frontend 31c3786a6. (1) `node frontend/scripts/check-prd-traceability.mjs` -> EXIT 0: '=== PRD traceability — 195 criteria, 36 tickets ===  manifest rows 195 · ticket criteria 195 · checked 0 · unchecked 195' then 'PASS — every criterion has exactly one owner, quoted verbatim, with matching state.' (2) `node frontend/scripts/check-prd-traceability-self-test.mjs` -> EXIT 0, '27/27 cases', 'PASS — the gate bites on every defect class it claims to cover.' The 27 cases each mutate a fixture tree and assert exit 1 with the right reason, and they cover exactly the clauses the criterion names: 'a PRD criterion loses its manifest row — exit 1 UNOWNED'; 'a criterion is assigned to two tickets — exit 1 DUPLICATE OWNER'; 'a ticket claims acceptance work that is in no PRD criterion — exit 1 TICKET-ONLY'; and ten separate cases, one per pinned id, 'restored module evidence PRD-C115/C118/C119/C123/C124/C125/C126/C127/C132/C136 is deleted rather than ticked — exit 1 RESTORED EVIDENCE DELETED'. (3) The three fail-open holes the prior report (reports/01-audit.md, verdict 'partially-met') found have all been closed since: F1 (37 id-less PRD checkbox lines invisible to the gate) is now section 1b, which freezes those 37 by content — 'UNIDENTIFIED CRITERION un-ticked', 'UNIDENTIFIED CRITERION' for a new id-less line, and 'LEGACY CRITERION DELETED' — all three self-tested. F2 (MIN_CRITERIA/MIN_TICKETS unpinned inside the gate) is now tied to the manifest's own prose headline via MANIFEST_HEADLINE, with 'MANIFEST HEADLINE DRIFT', 'VACUITY FLOOR LOWERED' and 'MANIFEST HEADLINE MISSING' self-tested. F4 (only 1 of the 10 restored ids self-tested) is fixed: RESTORED_MODULE_EVIDENCE moved into scripts/check-prd-traceability-pins.mjs and the self-test now generates one deletion case per key, which is why the self-test is 27/27 rather than the 10/10 the prior report saw. (4) It is wired blocking in CI: .github/workflows/frontend.yml:535 `run: pnpm run check:prd-traceability:self-test && pnpm run check:prd-traceability`, inside the `gates` job (line 262) which carries NO `needs:`, with `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` so a red Lint or a red earlier gate step cannot skip it. (5) The guarded corpus is committed, so CI can read it: `git ls-files .scratch/code-release-10-10-v2/issues/` = 36 files (== `ls`), and .scratch/code-release-10-10-v2/TRACEABILITY.md is tracked. 0 of 195 checkboxes are ticked, which is consistent — the gate enforces the mapping, not completion, and its own docstring says so: 'it cannot tell you whether a `[x]` is true'.
criteria.clauses_failing: None. RESIDUAL CAVEAT, not a failing clause: the workflow's `push` trigger carries `paths: [frontend/**, .github/workflows/frontend.yml]`, and none of the three guarded files (architecture-refactor/PRD-10-10-CODE-RELEASE-TODO.md, .scratch/.../TRACEABILITY.md, .scratch/.../issues/*.md) sits under those paths — I found 2 commits in the last 60 on this branch (94c7fda2c 'docs(release): per-ticket evidence reports and status lines', 299e925d1 'docs: remove release ticket scope overlap') that touch a guarded file and no frontend/** file, so a direct push of either would not have started the workflow. The `pull_request: branches: [main]` trigger has NO paths filter, so every PR to main does run the gate; the gap is direct-push-only. Adding the three paths to the push filter would close it. This does not make the gate fail-open — the gate never exits 0 over a defect in any of the 27 measured mutations.
